result.text: An a-fortiori argument transfers a claim from one ordered case to a stronger case using an independently justified monotonic warrant.
Amplificatio develops emphasis through elaboration, comparison, accumulation or restatement.
Apologia defends or explains a position or conduct; it is not necessarily an apology in the modern remorse sense.
Rhetorical apostrophe addresses an absent person, abstraction or entity as present; it is not the punctuation mark.
Apposition places a renaming or explanatory expression alongside another referring expression.
Common topics include comparison, definition, division, cause, consequence and circumstance as invention resources.
Concessio yields a limited point while retaining or reframing a larger claim.
Erasmus De copia treats abundance and variation in expression and subject matter as rhetorical exercises.
Deliberative rhetoric typically addresses future action through expediency, benefit and harm.
Aristotle relates dialectic and rhetoric as capacities for examining arguments in different settings rather than identical formal sciences.
Dilemma refutation may challenge the conditional premises, reject exhaustive horns or supply a counter-dilemma.
Dispositio concerns arranging material; a common teaching order is exordium, narratio, partitio, confirmatio, refutatio, peroratio.
Elocutio concerns verbal style, diction, figures and expression of selected material.
Encomium develops praise and invective blame, often through selected ancestry, acts, character or comparisons.
Epideictic rhetoric typically concerns praise/blame and communal values, often emphasizing the present.
Exordium introduces the discourse and can orient attention, context and audience relations.
Forensic rhetoric typically addresses past actions and questions of accusation, defence and justice.
Illustrators accompany speech content; emblems have independently conventionalized meanings within communities.
Hyperbaton broadly names departure from expected word order, often separating associated elements.
Hyperbole intentionally exaggerates; appropriateness depends on genre, audience, context and factual stakes.
Hysteron proteron presents a logically or temporally later element before an earlier one.
Innuendo conveys an implied suggestion without straightforward assertion.
Inventio concerns finding available arguments, questions, evidence and lines of appeal.
Kairos concerns situated opportunity and timing relative to audience and circumstance.
A gnome or maxim is a generalizing compact assertion about conduct or life; context and warrant remain important.
Meiosis reduces or minimizes how a matter is described, often for understatement or belittlement.
Memoria concerns preparing recall; classical locus methods associate material with independently selected ordered places.
Metanoia revises or corrects an expression, often restating it with greater precision or force.
Metonymy substitutes a contextually associated term, such as a container for its contents.
Narratio presents the account of circumstances or facts needed for the argument.
Onomatopoeia uses conventionally sound-imitating lexical forms; inventories differ by language and community.

Pronuntiatio or actio concerns delivery through voice and bodily presentation.
Reductio assumes a proposition and derives an independently established unacceptable consequence or contradiction.

Rogerian teaching emphasizes fair statement of an opposing position, contexts of validity, shared ground and a proposed accommodation.
